title: What if Jupiter became a star? 🔴
subject: jupiter
description:
Would you want a red second sun in your night sky? 👇

What would happen to Earth if Jupiter became a star? It would need about 80 times its mass to become a red dwarf like TRAPPIST-1. Physicists estimate it would outshine the full Moon and light up the night, but barely warm Earth at all.

Sources: BBC Science Focus, "Could Jupiter become a star?" (Dr Alastair Gunn, Jodrell Bank); EarthSky, "Is Jupiter a failed star?"; BBC Sky at Night, "Is Jupiter a failed star?" (2025); NASA, TRAPPIST-1 system; Ask a Mathematician, "How close is Jupiter to being a star? What would happen to us if it were?" (2011); Business Insider, "Jupiter came this close to being Earth's second blood-red sun" (2016).

scenes.text: You could read a book outside at midnight.
That's if Jupiter became a star. It would need about 80 times its mass to fuse hydrogen.
It would be a red dwarf, like TRAPPIST-1.
At its closest, it's 4 times farther than the Sun. Physicists estimate it would be a blood-red point 80 times brighter than the full Moon.
Earth would get just 0.02 percent more energy.
But for months every year, our nights would glow red.
